CASE: Memphis Light, Gas & Water Division v. Craft, 436 U.S. 1 (1978)
FACTS: episodes/_planning/EP64_memphis_FACTS_LEDGER.v001.md (WRITTEN 2026-08-04: 122 fact lines, 109 verbatim, 17 quarantined, all from measurements/EP64_memphis_RAW.md)

RESOLVED 2026-08-04 (was: ledger not written). The ledger is written from the 61,774-character opinion at measurements/EP64_memphis_RAW.md (CourtListener cluster 109855; 436 U.S. 1, filed 1978-05-01). THREE FINDINGS FROM THAT LEDGER BIND THE SCRIPT: (1) the opinion CONTRADICTS ITSELF on who failed to merge the accounts -- the majority says a contractor the Crafts hired, a footnote citing respondents' brief says the utility -- and on the number of terminations (majority: five; dissent: 'several'). The Court never resolved either, so the script may not pick a side. (2) NOBODY EVER DECIDED WHETHER THE CRAFTS OWED THE MONEY, so 'they were overcharged' is not available. (3) the Court expressly preserved the utility's power to cut service after a hearing -- verbatim: the utility 'would retain the option to terminate service after affording the notice and hearing required' -- so 'a hearing before shutoff' must never be told as 'shutoff was stopped'. Stevens's dissent is strong and quotable; use it so the film is not one-sided.

RETRIEVAL NOTE for anyone re-fetching: a plain search for 'Memphis Light' on the Supreme Court returns 408 results and NONE of them is this case — they are all later Tennessee workers-compensation matters. The query that works is the exact case name with the ampersand plus filed_after=1977 / filed_before=1979.

CourtListener's copy has no syllabus. If the episode needs one it must come from elsewhere.
